world._startX: Where a new run starts (the middle of the Coral Sea). The world loops: x = 0 and x = width are the same place.
world._loopOverlap: Scenery within this many px of the world's edges is copied past the other edge, so the loop is seamless at every zoom.
world._populationScale: Reef fish counts (balance population) are multiplied by this for the whole world. Scaled with the sea (114000 px) to keep the same density; fish far from the player sleep (ai.sleepDistance), so only the nearby ones cost time.

terrain._comment: Shape of the sea. Ground: sand dunes everywhere, rocky ridges, and seamounts whose flat tops (top = share of the water, 0 surface, 1 seabed) reach into the Reef with coral gardens. Islands break the surface; their sandbank (depth, px) is solid and their mangrove roots (rootsDepth) are a hiding place. Keep the player start (world center) clear.

regions._comment: Regions of the looping sea, left to right. Water colors: surface, Reef band, Deep band, seabed. Neighbors blend over `blend` px.

gates._comment: Gates between regions. Each wall spans the whole water column and is solid for the player (fish slip through) until it breaks. It can only be broken after beating the Tide's Checkpoint Crab (crabLevel >= crab): bite it (EAT at the wall) or ram it (swim into it fast, or dash). Broken gates are saved with the run; saves from before gates keep the whole sea open.
gates._ram: A ram counts when the speed aimed at the wall is above ramSpeedRatio x your cruising speed (or you dash). The wall bounces you back (bounce), so holding forward keeps ramming it.

scenery._comment: Scenery on the ground (x in world px; sits on the ground line there). Pieces in 'hide' are hiding places. 'arch' is solid rock you can swim through. Vents slowly heal the player (healPerSecond = share of max health). Floats bob at the surface. Keep pieces off steep seamount walls.

dayNight._comment: Day and night: four periods that blend smoothly (blendSeconds, centered on each change). Each period: sky and water tint colors, light rays, darkness around the player, stars, plankton glow, and gameplay: how far prey and predators see, how fast predators get hungry, how much plankton (zooplankton rise at night), how sleepy small fish are. A new run starts at startAt.

night.name: Night
night.line: Dark water: sneak and hide. Plankton rises and glows

growth._levelHardness: Each level needs this much more XP on top of the normal curve, compounding (0.03 = 3%: about +30% by level 10, 2.3x by level 30). Food fills the stomach the same, so you eat more per level.
growth._levelHardnessMaxLevels: The extra step stops compounding after this many levels (endless levels would otherwise explode); later levels still need more each time through the normal curve.
growth._levelStepMin: Every level needs at least this much more XP than the level before (0.15 = 15%), up to levelHardnessMaxLevels. Early levels already grow faster than this; from about level 13 each level is 15% harder. After the cap, levels keep growing with the normal curve (a few % each), so endless levels stay reachable.

biomes._comment: How much each species likes each region (0 = never there). A species' fish are shared out by weight x region width; they wander mostly where they like it. Missing = 1 everywhere.

spawnDefaults._comment: Spawn factors every enemy starts from (see "spawnFactors" for each one, and "biomes" / species spawn depths for where). activity = share of them out at each time of day; waveEvery/waveStay = they come in waves (0 = always there); respawnDelay = seconds before an eaten one comes back; nearPlayer = chance a respawn appears just off your screen; roam = how far (px) it wanders while it likes the region; perTide = extra share of the count each Tide; groupMin/groupMax = spawns in groups; maxHunters = most that hunt you at once (0 = no limit); levelMin/levelMax = spawn levels (plus the Tide bonus); eliteChance/eliteLevels = a rare golden one, that many levels stronger; lastLevel = it leaves the sea after this level (0 = never).

spawnFactors._comment: Each enemy's own spawn factors (only what differs from "spawnDefaults"). Real-life habits: nocturnal hunters are out more at night, schooling fish come in schools, pack hunters in packs.

ai._camo: A camouflaged animal (species camo, the octopus) moving slower than camoStillSpeed fades to camoAlpha and is hidden from fish farther than kelpSeeThroughDistance x its size.
ai._gridCell: Size (px) of the cells of the grid that brains use to find nearby creatures (rebuilt each frame).
ai._sleepDistance: Fish farther than this (px, sideways) from the player sleep: no thinking, no physics, not drawn. They wake up where they were when the player comes near.

combat._ramSlowRankRatio: Ramming a fish slows you (half speed) only if it is clearly stronger than you (rank above 1.25x yours, like the threat rule); anything else is just knocked aside. Rams and rock stuns count the speed aimed into the target, not a graze.

stomach._capacityStepMin: Each level the stomach holds at least this much more than the level before (0.15 = 15%), up to capacityStepMaxLevels; after that it grows with the normal curve. A bigger stomach takes more food to fill.
stomach._digestTo: After digesting, the stomach drops to this share (0.15 = nearly empty), so you have to eat a lot again.
stomach._biteScrapXpFraction: Meat torn off by a bite (the fish still alive) does not fill the stomach: it only gives this share of its XP right away. Kill the fish and eat the carcass to fill up.

stages._comment: Player growth by stage. body = [size at the first level, size at the last level] (look, physics, what fits in the mouth). rank = how strong the reef thinks you are (who hunts, who flees, health and bite). Both grow a little inside a stage and jump when you evolve.
stages._maxLevel: Practical cap only: levels are endless. Past the last stage (adult, level 30) are Legend levels: the body stays adult-sized, strength grows a little each level.

dart.name: Dart
dart.label: DART
dart._comment: Mosa's hatchling dash: the same as Lunge.

earlyHelp._comment: A head start for new hatchlings: at levels up to fullUntil you swim faster, turn quicker, sprint longer (stamina = drain multiplier) and take less damage. It fades out evenly until endsAt, after which you play with your normal stats. Stacks with perks.

perks._comment: Pick 1 of 3 perks at these levels (twice per stage, never on an evolution level). Perks stack.

list.name: Big Belly
list.desc: Stomach holds 25% more and empties 10% slower.

areas._comment: Depth bands of the sea, as a share of the water from the surface (0) to the seabed (1). A stage can swim down to its maxDepth; below that a current pushes it back up.

heroes._comment: Playable heroes. Each one shares the stage levels, sizes, ranks and depths in 'stages' and swaps in its own species (speed, armor), stage designs and abilities.

crocodile.name: Croc
crocodile.blurb: Tough hide. Shell Guard, Lunge, Death Roll.

mosa.name: Mosa
mosa.blurb: Fast swimmer, thinner hide. Dart, Tail Slam, Crushing Bite.

white_shark.name: Shark
white_shark.blurb: Hardest bite, thin skin. Dart, Lunge, Feeding Frenzy.

checkpointCrab._comment: A Checkpoint Crab appears every `everyLevels` levels. Defeat it and that level is saved: after dying you swim again from it (instead of from level 1). Its strength is set from yours when it appears, so the fight is fair for every hero and perk: it takes about `hitsToDefeat` of your bites, and each pinch takes `pinchHpFraction` of your health and stuns you briefly. It stays around its spot (`homeWidth` x `homeHeight`) near the deepest water you may swim in, and chases you only within `guardRange`.

tides._comment: A Tide is a chapter of `levelsPerTide` levels, ending with the Checkpoint Crab. Themes repeat as harder '+' versions after the list runs out. Each Tide from the 2nd on, reef fish spawn `aiLevelsPerTide` levels higher (up to `aiLevelBonusMax`). Legend levels (past the adult stage): strength x(1 + legendRankPerLevel) per level, and a perk every `legendPerkEvery` levels.

music._comment: Soundtrack moods. 'sunny' is the recorded CC0 track (Aquaria); the others are generated live (scale = semitones, root = MIDI key note, bpm, how busy the melody/bass/pad/ticks are). The game picks a mood from region, time of day, depth and the Checkpoint Crab; each Tide shifts the key. When hunted, a low pulse joins.

land._comment: Leaving the water: sprint up through the surface faster than jumpSpeed to leap out. Gravity pulls you down; land on an island (sand hump, mangrove mud, iceberg) and crawl left/right; swim up + sprint to hop. Out of the water you dry out: after drySafeSeconds you lose dryDamagePerSecond of max health each second.

regionTwists._comment: Each region plays a little differently (src/systems/regionTwists.ts). 1 = no change. vision: how far every fish sees; food: plankton amount; hunger and speed: the player's; ventHeal: warm vent healing; ventWarms: resting by a vent cancels the hunger and speed twist. current: px/s pushing everything east (Sargasso Drift). dark: darkness around the player day and night, plankton glows (Trench, 0 to 1). bigSlow: speed of creatures above juvenile size there (Kelp Forest).

swamp.hint: Murky water: everyone sees less, and food is everywhere

volcano.hint: Hot water: you get hungry faster, but vents heal twice as much

ice.hint: Cold water: you swim slower and get hungry faster. Warm up by a vent

sargasso.hint: Open water: hide under the floating weed. A current pushes you east

trench.hint: Dark water: everyone sees half as far. Glowing fish give themselves away

kelp.hint: Tangled kelp: hiding everywhere, but big bodies swim slower
